newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ARGENTINA GAIN REVENGE OVER COLOMBIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA GAIN REVENGE OVER COLOMBIA.

text.p: Argentina gained revenge for one of their greatest soccer humiliations when they beat Colombia 1-0 away in the South American World Cup qualifiers on Wednesday.

Argentina, with a 5-0 home defeat against the same opponents in 1993 stuck in their throats, ended Colombia's unbeaten run in the competition and allowed them to get their own campaign back on the rails after some poor results.

As the marathon competition -- in which all the South American nations have been thrown into the same group and play each other twice -- reached the halfway mark, Paraguay went level on points with Colombia at the top.
The Paraguayans took full advantage of Colombia's slip by beating Peru 2-1 at home and now trail Colombia only on goal difference.
Aristides Rojas scored the winner two minutes before halftime for Paraguay, who play five of their remaining eight games in their intimidating "Defenders of the Chaco" stadium.

Argentina's win put them third, one point ahead of unfancied Ecuador, who caused a stunning upset with a 4-0 thrashing of Uruguay, one of international soccer's traditional powers. The Uruguayans had three players sent off near the end, by which time the result had been settled.
The top four teams will qualify for France, while Brazil are excused the marathon as reigning champions.
A bizarre mistake by goalkeeper Farid Mondragon allowed Claudio Lopez to score the ninth-minute goal which handed Colombia their first home World Cup defeat in 12 years.
Mondragon thought that Lopez's innocuous-looking 25-metre effort was going out of play and casually let it past him only to see it bounce into the net. "The ball had a strange spin on it," he said.
The 60,000 crowd in Barranquilla also their team saw squander a one-man advantage for the whole of the second half and miss a penalty in the 54th minute.
Argentine defender Eduardo Berizzo was sent off in the 45th minute for a foul while Colombia midfielder Mauricio Serna missed the target altogether with his effort from the penalty spot.
Although Colombia dominated the midfield, striker Faustino Asprilla suffered an off-day while Argentina packed their defence effectively.
Both nations came to a standstill for the game, with shops and offices shutting, and thousands ran onto the streets of Buenos Aires at the end to celebrate Argentina's triumph.

While Colombia struggled, Francisco Maturana, the man who led them to the last two World Cups, saw his current team Ecuador -- yet to play in the World Cup finals -- hammer Uruguay at altitude in Quito.
Alex Aguinaga fired Ecuador ahead from close range in the sixth minute to set Uruguay on the slippery slope to defeat.
Two goals by Agustin Delgado in an eight-minute spell in the second half sealed the game, with substitute Kleber Chala adding a fourth in the 88th minute.
Uruguay, warned by soccer's governing body FIFA about their behaviour after having seven men booked against Chile last year, this time had three sent off.

Gustavo Mendez was dismissed for a violent tackle and Daniel Fonseca and Nelson Abeijon for arguing with Argentine referee Javier Castrilli - known as "lawman" in his own country for his hardline approach.
The result left Uruguay in fifth place and in danger of failing to qualify for the second World Cup running.
In the other game, Bolivia dropped two more home points when they were held to a 1-1 draw by Chile in La Paz.

Bolivia had expected the altitude of their capital, which lies 3,600 metres above sea level, to give them a springboard for qualification but have drawn four of their six games played at home, leaving them one point behind Uruguay.
